To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) day capacitance was best predicted by wood density and predawn lumentic volumetric water content; 2) vessel-ray contact fraction was the strongest anatomical predictor; 3) wood was less than full saturated at predawn for all species; 4) capacitance was not explained by tissue lumen fractions or tissue-specific water contents.

Wood capacitance is related both to the amount of water stored in wood (wood density and water content) and the anatomical structure of wood (vessel-tissue contact area) and this is true across a wide diversity of temperate tree species.
Wood day capacitance is a function of wood water content and wood density.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of capacitance and how these vary with anatomy and wood structure.
how wood anatomy influences the ability of trees to store water and how this influences their drought response.
the role of wood in plant water relations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
capacitance is a function of water storage capacity (wood density and water content) and the connectivity of the water transport system.

the capacitance of wood is a function of water content, wood anatomy (e.g. vessel dimensions, tissue proportions, vessel-tissue contact fraction) and bulk wood properties (e.g. wood density) and that the relative importance of these factors varies with the species and the type of porous wood.

capacitance is related not only to the amount of stored (capable) water, but also to the connectivity and the bulk properties of wood, and that this relationship differs between diffuse- and semi/ring-porosity species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
capacitance is not a property of any particular tissue, but a function of the bulk wood properties, which are a function of the amount of stored (capacitve) water, and the connectivity of tissues.
day capacitance is determined by the amount of stored wood water (VWCL), tissue connectivity, and bulk wood properties (e.g., wood density).
day capacitance is a function of water content, wood properties (WD and tissue connectivity) and anatomy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the amount of water that is released from the stem of trees during the day is determined by the amount of water stored in the stem, the bulk properties arising from wood density, and the degree of tissue connectivity.
the capacitance of a tree species is related to its wood anatomy.

capacitance can be meaningfully predicted from a few wood anatomical and bulk wood properties, which could help to better understand how wood properties and anatomy affect tree water transport and drought response.
